name: Giant Crocodile
appearance: A giant crocodile that waits below the surface.

Attacks.name: Bite and tail smash
Attacks.effectNote: The bite deals 3–18 damage. The tail smash deals 2–20. It can still attack with its tail in a 180-degree arc behind it while holding prey.

Attacks.name: Surprise
Attacks.effectNote: The crocodile surprises on 1–3 on a d6.

Encounters.name: Buoyant pool ambush
Encounters.effectNote: It waits at either side of the buoyant pool for creatures avoiding the group in the center. In this encounter, only stabbing weapons affect it, and attacks against it take a −2 penalty because of the water.

Encounters.name: Drag underwater
Encounters.effectNote: The crocodile tries to take a bitten creature to the bottom. Drowning takes 2–4 rounds. The hold ends only after the crocodile takes at least 10 damage in total from hits. It then attacks another victim.

notes: Gary Gygax, Dungeonland (TSR, 1983), The Long Hall, changed view, p. 5.

name: Giant Poisonous Snake

habitats: The Woods of Trees and Giant Fungi

Special attacks.name: Poison
Special attacks.effectNote: The table gives 3–18 points of poison damage even on a successful save.

Encounters.name: Wandering monster table
Encounters.effectNote: A result of 2–3 gives one Giant Poisonous Snake with 26 HP.

notes: The table gives no separate failed-save outcome.
Gary Gygax, Dungeonland (TSR, 1983), The Woods of Trees and Giant Fungi, wandering monsters, p. 12.

name: Giant Dog
appearance: A furry dog nearly as large as an elephant.

Attacks.name: Grasping jaws
Attacks.effectNote: If harmed, the dog attacks. On an attack roll of 20 it grabs its target in its jaws and runs at twice its speed toward its place behind Area C. The held target takes an additional 2–12 damage per round. Once out of the party’s sight, the dog sits down and eats the captured creature.

Encounters.name: Playful approach
Encounters.effectNote: The dog approaches out of curiosity. While it sniffs and snaps playfully, it has a 1-in-20 chance to knock someone down for 1–6 damage.

Encounters.name: Rations or fetch
Encounters.effectNote: One week of ordinary rations or two weeks of iron rations gets it to rest and ignore the party. It plays with a thrown stick, staff, or pole for a turn and then goes to sleep near the forest edge.

Encounters.name: Ticks in the fur
Encounters.effectNote: Searching its fur reveals three Giant Ticks.

notes: The printed dog movement uses a single prime, 18′.
Gary Gygax, Dungeonland (TSR, 1983), The Wilds of Dungeonland, A. Meadow, p. 13.

name: Giant Tick
appearance: A giant tick found in the fur of the meadow’s Giant Dog.

Special attacks.name: Attachment and blood drain
Special attacks.effectNote: A hit attaches the tick to its target. The tick drains 1–6 points thereafter. A bitten character has a 50% chance of contracting a disease.

Encounters.name: Three ticks on the Giant Dog
Encounters.effectNote: A search of the dog’s fur turns up three ticks with 19, 18, and 17 HP respectively.

notes: The encounter gives no separate interval for the blood drain.
Gary Gygax, Dungeonland (TSR, 1983), The Wilds of Dungeonland, A. Meadow, p. 13.
